title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 1
paragraphs: The learned among the Persians say the Phoenicians were the ones who started the quarrel. They came, so the story goes, from what is called the Erythraean Sea to the Mediterranean, and once they had settled in the land where they still live today, they immediately began making long sea voyages. Carrying Egyptian and Assyrian merchandise, they traded in many places, and eventually reached Argos — which at that time was the leading state in what is now called Hellas. When the Phoenicians arrived at Argos, they began selling their cargo. On the fifth or sixth day, when nearly all their goods had been sold, a great crowd of women came down to the shore, and among them was the king's daughter, whose name, as the Hellenes also agree, was Io, daughter of Inachus. The women were standing near the ship's stern, buying whatever pleased them most, when the Phoenicians, passing the word among themselves, suddenly rushed at them. Most of the women escaped by running, but Io and a few others were seized, thrown aboard the ship, and carried off at once to Egypt.
